name: Mexico City International Airport (Benito Juárez)

permits.v: closed to private general aviation and air taxi since a presidential decree of 1 June 1994; the DGAC circular CO SA-30/12 allows only exceptions (flights requested by the Presidency, federal ministers and other listed officials, diplomats at the Foreign Ministry's request), for aircraft over 5,700 kg; requests at least 5 hours ahead, Mon-Fri 09:00-16:00, subject to space in the daily schedule, and not in the peak periods 07:00-10:00 and 19:00-22:00; the decree excludes military, presidential staff, air ambulance, emergency and rotary-wing aircraft and those the ministry authorises
permits.quote: el cierre de las operaciones en el AICM a la aviación privada, la aviación de estado y las operaciones de taxi aéreo

ppr.v: any exceptional general aviation flight needs DGAC (now AFAC) authorisation requested at least 5 hours before the flight and depends on space in the AICM daily schedule; no flights 07:00-10:00 and 19:00-22:00
ppr.quote: entre las 07:00 a 10:00 horas y de las 19:00 a 22:00 horas

slots.v: AFAC Bases Generales for Level 3 saturated airports (published after 9 Jun 2026; it cites the bases of 14 Oct 2025, repeal wording not read): for all hours declared saturated no slot may be assigned to Mexican XB private and third-party aircraft, or to foreign aircraft on international private, corporate, demonstration or ferry-for-import flights or on-demand air taxi. Excluded: head of the Federal Executive, national security, exclusively air ambulance or emergency services, rotary-wing. Passenger charter (fletamento) is listed among the slot-eligible non-scheduled services. Recitals give AICM airfield saturation 07:00-22:59 (declaration of 29 Sep 2014), Terminal 1 05:00-22:59 (resolution of 3 Mar 2022) and Terminal 2 06:00-10:59, 13:00-19:59, 21:00-21:59. Times as printed; local is the natural reading
slots.quote: Extranjeras con las características siguientes: a) Vuelos privados internacionales; b) Vuelos corporativos internacionales; ... e) Taxi aéreo para la modalidad de operaciones a demanda del usuario

notes: Mexico AIP (aipmexico.seneam.gob.mx, AD 2 MMMX, AMDT AIRAC 02/26: https://aipmexico.seneam.gob.mx/AIP/doc/AD/AD_2/38_MMMX/AD_2-MMMX-2.pdf) refused by the site (robots), so no runway, customs or hours data. The circular CO SA-30/12 (DGAC/SCT, in force from 17 May 2012, indefinite) is hosted on gob.mx; whether AFAC has amended it since was not checked. The circular does not say whether its times are local; local is the natural reading. AICM site pages read gave no runway or GA data. Practical meaning: private charter jets normally cannot use MMMX; offer Toluca (MMTO) or other airports. 1 Nov 2026: added slots from the AICM operator's Informe de Gestión Gubernamental 2018-2024 (dated 17 Sep 2024; the 2023 resolution's 43/hour cap applies 'en tanto prevalezcan las condiciones de saturación'). AIP AD 2 MMMX (https://aipmexico.seneam.gob.mx/AIP/doc/AD/AD_2/38_MMMX/AD_2-MMMX-2.pdf) still could not be opened (fetch tool blocked). Runway lengths not in the AICM documents read. | 3 Nov 2026: AIP AD 2 MMMX (https://aipmexico.seneam.gob.mx/AIP/doc/AD/AD_2/38_MMMX/AD_2-MMMX-2.pdf) again refused (robots); the owner should download it. Anexo 4 RGCE 2026 (DOF 14 Jan 2026, https://www.sat.gob.mx/minisitio/NormatividadRMFyRGCE/documentos2026/rgce/anexos/Anexo4delasRGCEpara2026.pdf) gives Aduana AICM Mon-Fri 08:00-20:00, Sat 10:00-14:00, but only for import and export of goods; not recorded as customs, because it does not say it covers private flight clearance. 5 Nov 2026: slots rule replaced with the newer AFAC Bases Generales Nivel 3 (sidof.segob.gob.mx docFuente 5796164). Publication date not visible in the text read; it cites a decree of 9 Jun 2026 and the Bases of 14 Oct 2025. The tool could not reach the transitorios (the last part of the page), so entry into force and repeal of the 2025 Bases were not read: confirm before relying on it. Same prohibition appears in the 14 Oct 2025 Bases (5769851). Only AICM is named as saturated in the recitals read. Earlier 2023 resolution's 43 per hour cap (mmmx-sacm-informe-2024) is not in the text read and remains from that report. One reading of the Terminal 2 hours labelled it a later (2025) resolution; the year was not confirmed, so check the current declaration. Base Tercera III(e) quote: 'Taxi aéreo para la modalidad de operaciones a demanda del usuario'. Base Cuarta quote: 'De transporte aéreo no regular bajo la modalidad de fletamento para pasajeros'; not limited to Mexican carriers in the text read, but whether a foreign on-demand jet can qualify as fletamento is unclear: treat as air taxi unless AFAC confirms. Unchanged: CO SA-30/12 permits and ppr. AIP AD 2 still refused (robots). Earlier slots rule, from the operator's 2024 report: every operation needs an assigned slot, and a DOF resolution of 31 Aug 2023 caps the airport at 43 take-offs and landings per hour from 8 Jan 2024. | 7 Nov 2026: nothing new. AIP AD 2 not retried (permission refused on aipmexico.seneam.gob.mx again today for MMSD). Searches on aicm.com.mx gave no runway or hours page. | 9 Nov 2026: read the AICM terminal capacity study published on aicm.com.mx (uploaded Aug 2026, https://www.aicm.com.mx/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3-2-EstudioCapacidad-V10-VPublica.pdf): no runway, hours or general aviation text; it speaks of the viability of 44 operations per hour and models 46 as a scenario only. Press reports (not citable) say the SICT authorised 46 operations per hour in 2026; no DOF text was found, so the 43/hour figure in the notes may be out of date: check the current DOF resolution. AIP AD 2 not retried (robots). Nothing added.
